svg.title: The lead session stopped after each request and waited for the person; an automated harness would close the loop and add its own checks

cc:Work.dc:title: The lead session stopped after each request and waited for the person; an automated harness would close the loop and add its own checks
cc:Work.dc:description: Two box-and-arrow diagrams, one above the other. Top, how this entry was run: a loop from the person, who sends a short request (about 110 in nine days), to the lead session (one session, its context summarised 21 times, a status log and a decision ledger as memory), to about 50 multi-agent workflows, to experiments on GPUs, to results and options written down, and back to the person, who uploads up to 5 files a day and passes the public score back. A marker in the person's box says that the loop waits there for the next message. Bottom, what an automated harness would add: a closed loop of five steps inside a frame, propose (checked against the catalogue of closed ideas), run (with a noise probe), evaluate (on validation and the holdout, under a rule written first), keep or drop, and archive, from which the next round starts without a message. Outside the frame stand the person, who sets the goal and the budget and uploads the files, a second model as critic, and a scheduled look back over the ledger.
